extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: DocVQA is a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images. It aims to inspire a “purpose-driven” point of view in Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research, where an intelligent reading system responds to ad-hoc requests for information expressed in natural language questions by human users. Answering questions in DocVQA requires models not just to read text but interpret it within the layout/structure of the document, exploiting visual cues like layout, non-textual elements, and style.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images for the dataset are sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from various collections, and specific pages were hand-picked for inclusion. Efforts were made to minimize binarized images due to quality concerns and to prioritize pages containing tables, forms, lists, and figures over those with only running text. Questions and answers for these selected document images were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool, following a three-stage annotation process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Documents from UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Pages from the UCSF Industry Documents Library were hand-picked, with a focus on minimizing binarized images and prioritizing pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures. During the second annotation stage, questions deemed inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were flagged by workers and excluded from the dataset. In the third review stage, authors reviewed questions with answer mismatches, editing questions and answers as necessary before acceptance or ignoring them.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (question-answer pairs) were collected in three stages using a web-based annotation tool by remote workers. In Stage 1, workers defined up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image, encouraged to provide multiple ground truth answers if warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions answerable by text in the image and to enter answers verbatim, making it an extractive QA problem. In Stage 2, workers were shown images and questions from Stage 1 (without answers) and asked to enter answers and assign one or more question types. They could also flag inapt questions. In Stage 3, questions with answer mismatches between Stage 1 and 2 were reviewed by the authors, who could edit questions/answers or add new ones before acceptance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in the first stage matched exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question was sent for review in a third stage. This third stage review was done by the authors themselves, who could edit questions and answers or add new answers before accepting the question.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: at most 10 question-answer pairs per document image
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to inspire a “purpose-driven” approach in document image analysis and recognition research. It motivates the simultaneous use of visual and textual cues for answering questions on document images, which could drive methods utilizing low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) to solve problems of practical importance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The source documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library contain binarized images, which can negatively impact image quality, potentially serving as a bottleneck for VQA despite efforts to minimize them. OCR errors are a known issue, leading to incorrect answers even when models correctly ground questions, and can cause problems like over-segmentation of text. Minor mismatches between human-entered answers and ground truth also occur.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images, Document Analysis and Recognition (DAR) research
